text: G.S.R.843(E), clause (c), commences the main processing, child-data and rights provisions eighteen months after publication; clause (b) puts Consent Manager provisions at one year. Final Rules rule 1 staggers commencement similarly. **Inference:** The later tranches fall in May 2027 and November 2026 respectively; neither milestone has arrived on this brief's date. Exact day-level dates remain unresolved here because the printed Gazette masthead says 13 November 2025 while the electronic code/listing indicates 14 November, and publication is the legal trigger. Institution/Board provisions already commenced do not make the entire framework operative.

text: The Act defines personal data by identifiability, not whether the application calls a record synthetic. **Inference:** Wholly fictitious, non-linkable fixtures do not identify a real individual; actual accounts, uploaded documents, network logs or analytics can still contain personal data. Synthetic business records alone therefore do not establish that an online deployment handles no personal data.

text: Section 4 permits consent or specified legitimate uses; s.6 confines consent to necessary data for the stated purpose. Conversely, asserting that every processing step always requires a fresh consent is also too broad.

text: **Fact about future substantive duties:** Section 8(7) requires erasure at withdrawal/purpose completion subject to legally necessary retention. Final r.8(3) requires minimum one-year retention of processing data, traffic and logs for Seventh Schedule purposes, followed by erasure unless further lawful retention applies; r.6(1)(e) also addresses security retention. These DPDP provisions have not commenced as of 28 October 2026; this is not an already-universal one-year retention rule. **Sources:** [Act](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/Digital-Personal-Data-Protection-Act-2023-1
